title: Why Asians Never Wear Shoes Inside
description: Ever been yelled at for wearing shoes inside an Asian home? There's a 3,000-year-old reason your grandma was right all along.

sections.narration: Walk into any Asian home with your shoes on... and watch what happens.
sections.visual_notes: Stick figure at a doorway, one foot stepping inside with a shoe on, shocked faces in background

sections.narration: Your grandma didn't make this rule because she was being difficult. She was being a genius.
sections.visual_notes: Stick figure grandma with arms crossed, pointing at shoes, looking stern but wise

sections.narration: In many Asian households, wearing shoes inside is treated like a crime. You'll get the look. You'll get the lecture.
sections.visual_notes: Stick figure getting scolded, red angry marks around grandma's head, shoes with X marks

sections.narration: This tradition goes back over three thousand years in Japan, where floors were for sitting, sleeping, and eating.
sections.visual_notes: Ancient Japanese room with tatami mats, stick figure sitting on floor eating, shoes outside door

sections.narration: Your floor was your table, your bed, and your chair. Shoes on that? Disgusting.
sections.visual_notes: Split image: floor as dining table on left, floor as bed on right, dirty shoe print in center with X

sections.narration: Modern science proved grandma right. A University of Arizona study found that shoes carry over four hundred thousand bacteria per shoe.
sections.visual_notes: Stick figure scientist looking at shoe under magnifying glass, green bacteria everywhere, number 400,000

sections.narration: Including E. coli. On ninety-six percent of shoes tested. Your grandma didn't need a lab to figure that out.
sections.visual_notes: Stick figure grandma smugly crossing arms, pie chart showing 96%, bacteria icons around shoe

sections.narration: And it's not just Asia. In Finland, Canada, and most of the Middle East, shoes come off at the door. Always.
sections.visual_notes: World map with shoes-off countries highlighted, stick figures in different cultural clothing all removing shoes

sections.narration: The twist? Americans wearing shoes inside is actually the global minority. Most of the world thinks it's gross.
sections.visual_notes: Stick figure in American flag shirt looking confused, surrounded by other stick figures pointing and looking shocked

sections.narration: So next time someone says take your shoes off... just do it. Three thousand years of wisdom can't be wrong.
sections.visual_notes: Stick figure happily placing shoes at doorway, grandma giving thumbs up, clean floor sparkles
